executiveAtAGlance.thesisHeadline: Veeva's dominant life sciences vertical SaaS platform, four-quarter EPS beat streak, and $1.3B net cash position are priced at a near-trough multiple following a sentiment-driven de-rating.

summaryParagraphs: Veeva Systems is the dominant cloud software platform for life sciences, with embedded switching costs, a recurring revenue model, and a balance sheet carrying net cash of $1.3B. The stock has been cut in half from its 52-week high of $310.50, presenting a compelling entry point for investors with a 2–3 year horizon.

At 15.3x forward P/E and 5.7x EV/Revenue on consensus FY27E revenue of $3.6B, VEEV trades at a material discount to its 5-year average multiples despite improving profitability. Our $225 price target is derived from a blended 50/50 DCF/comps methodology, implying +48.6% upside from current levels.
catalysts: CRM to Vault CRM migration: ongoing conversion of the legacy Salesforce-based CRM base onto Vault CRM drives incremental ARPU expansion and deepens platform lock-in.
Beat-and-raise cadence: VEEV has beaten EPS consensus for four consecutive quarters, validating structural earnings power above Street estimates.
Margin expansion runway: operating margin expanded from 18.2% in FY24 to 28.7% in FY26, with consensus projecting continued improvement as Vault platform mix rises.
primaryRisks: Citigroup downgrade: Citi cut VEEV to Neutral from Buy on April 10, 2026, slashing its PT to $176 from $291, citing growth and valuation concerns.
Biopharma R&D budget pressure: macro headwinds and ongoing FDA and NIH funding uncertainty could slow clinical trial software spend among smaller biotech customers.
AI narrative risk: investor debate around whether AI tooling disrupts Veeva's data and workflow moat before management can monetize it is weighing on sentiment.
executiveSummary.valuationBridge: At 15.3x forward P/E and 5.7x EV/Revenue, Veeva trades at a material discount to its own history despite improving profitability, supporting a blended valuation that still points to substantial upside.

summaryParagraphs: Revenue compounded at approximately 14% over three years, with FY26 marking an acceleration to 16.3% YoY growth as Vault platform migrations gained traction. Gross margin expanded from 71.3% in FY23 to 75.5% in FY26, driven by subscription mix shift and operating leverage on shared platform infrastructure.
highlights: FY26 revenue was $3.195B vs. $2.747B in FY25, up 16.3% YoY.
FY26 operating income was $916.4M, an operating margin of 28.7%, up from 25.2% in FY25.
FY26 net income was $908.9M, for a 28.4% net margin vs. 26.0% in FY25.
Q4 FY26 quarterly revenue of $836.0M represented sequential growth of 3.1% from Q3.

summaryParagraphs: Veeva's balance sheet is a fortress. Net cash stood at $1.325B as of January 31, 2026, up from $1.043B a year prior. Total equity has compounded from $3.7B to $7.2B over three years, driven entirely by retained earnings.

FCF generation has compounded at approximately 22% annually over the past three fiscal years, reaching $1.415B in FY26. FCF margin of 44.3% in FY26 ranks among the highest in enterprise software. Return metrics have improved materially as the FY24 investment cycle concluded.
highlights: FY26 operating cash flow was $1.415B vs. $1.090B in FY25, up 29.8% YoY.
FY26 FCF margin was 44.3% of revenue, up from 39.7% in FY25.
TTM FCF from locked data was $1.048B, reflecting timing differences versus annual figures.
FY26 ROIC improved to 13.5%, clearly above the company's cost of capital.

summaryParagraphs: VEEV trades at a significant discount to its own historical averages across nearly every metric. At 15.3x forward P/E, the stock is pricing in minimal growth optionality, a stark contrast to the 30x to 40x forward multiples the company commanded in 2021–2023.

The DCF uses a 5-year explicit forecast period anchored to FY26 actuals as the base year. Assumptions reflect a conservative deceleration in growth from 16% toward 11–12% as the company scales, with operating margins stabilizing at 30–33% as Vault platform mix normalizes.

valuation.valuationConclusion: VEEV is undervalued on both a multiples and intrinsic value basis. At $151.43, the stock is pricing in bear-case assumptions for a company that just delivered 16.3% revenue growth and 28.7% operating margins with four straight EPS beats.

summaryParagraphs: Veeva operates across two broad platform verticals: Commercial Cloud and Research & Development Cloud. Both are subscription-based with strong revenue visibility, while the Vault platform underpins both verticals and is the primary architectural differentiator.

Veeva possesses a wide economic moat anchored primarily by switching costs and life-sciences-specific regulatory requirements. No horizontal SaaS vendor has successfully replicated its domain depth in pharma compliance workflows.

moatTable.title: Economic Moat Assessment
rows: GxP-validated systems require extensive requalification; migration risk deters switching.
Preferred vendor across top 20 global pharma; reference customers drive sales cycles.
Veeva Network HCP data grows in value with scale; Vault ecosystem creates cross-module stickiness.
Domain-specific data models and compliance templates are hard to replicate quickly.
Shared Vault infrastructure creates cost leverage unavailable to smaller point-solution vendors.
FDA and EMA compliance requirements raise the bar for new entrants building validated systems.

economicMoatAssessment.overallMoatConclusion: Veeva appears to have a wide moat. High switching costs in regulated GxP environments, a sticky data network, and years of life-sciences-specific product development create barriers that horizontal CRM or document-management vendors cannot easily overcome.

nearTermCatalysts: Vault CRM migrations should accelerate through FY27, driving ARPU uplift and reducing Salesforce-related economics leakage.
Q1 FY27 revenue consensus of $857.7M implies +13.0% YoY growth, with upside potential given the beat cadence.
The RegASK partnership expands RIM Intelligence capabilities and may accelerate R&D Cloud wins.
mediumTermDrivers: International expansion in Asia-Pacific and emerging markets.
Cross-sell of Quality and Safety modules to existing Vault Clinical customers.
Vault EDC and Veeva Site Connect expansion.
longTermOpportunities: Adjacent vertical expansion into animal health, chemicals, and consumer products.
Becoming the operating system for regulated industries beyond pharma.
Monetization of the Veeva Network and Veeva Compass datasets.

summaryParagraphs: Veeva's TAM across life sciences is substantial and underpenetrated. Management's existing product suite serves a large software opportunity across commercial workflows, R&D, and adjacent regulated industries.
highlights: Commercial Cloud TAM is about $4B–$5B globally.
R&D Cloud TAM is about $5B–$6B across clinical, regulatory, quality, and safety workflows.
Adjacent verticals add another $3B–$4B of incremental TAM.
Veeva's current penetration still leaves meaningful runway across both core and adjacent markets.

summaryParagraphs: Founder and CEO Peter Gassner has led Veeva since inception in 2007 and remains a central strategic asset. His founder-operator status, deep domain expertise, and large equity stake create strong long-term alignment.

Management has been disciplined and conservative in capital allocation. The company has avoided large, dilutive M&A, self-funded product development organically, and preserved a strong net-cash balance sheet.

Insider ownership is substantial and dominated by Gassner's stake, creating strong economic alignment. The dual-class structure preserves long-cycle strategic control, while executive compensation includes meaningful long-term equity components.

rows: Phased rollout, migration tooling, and management track record
Long-term contracts and high switching costs post-validation
Vault platform breadth and ability to embed AI into workflows
Fundamental value floor and beat cadence
Large pharma base is less discretionary; long contracts
Mission-critical compliance software is last to be cut

finalRecommendation.valuationMethodology: Price target of $225 derived from a blended 50% DCF base case and 50% peer NTM P/E comps methodology.

ratingChangeTriggers.trigger: Stock declines below $145, or management raises FY27 guidance above $3.75B revenue with Vault CRM migration tracking ahead of schedule, or a significant buyback program is announced.
Stock appreciates above $215, or R&D Cloud growth decelerates below 15% for two consecutive quarters, or Vault CRM migration falls more than one full quarter behind schedule.
FY27 revenue guidance below $3.50B, or subscription revenue growth falls below 10% for two consecutive quarters, or evidence of competitive share loss to IQVIA or Salesforce in new enterprise RFPs.

finalRecommendation.closingParagraph: Veeva's 52-week decline has created a fundamentally disconnected setup: a company with 16% revenue growth, 75% gross margins, $1.3B net cash, and four consecutive EPS beats is trading at a near-trough forward multiple. The current valuation appears to price in risks that are unlikely to materialize at the magnitude implied.

openQuestions: What percentage of the legacy Salesforce-based CRM base has migrated to Vault CRM as of Q1 FY27, and what is management's revised completion timeline?
How is Veeva's R&D Cloud pipeline tracking in the context of biopharma budget tightening?
What is Q1 FY27 RPO growth, and does it signal an acceleration or deceleration versus FY26 revenue growth?
Has management provided any update on a formal share repurchase authorization given the current valuation?
How quickly can Vault CRM economics improve as Salesforce-related licensing costs roll off?
Are smaller biotech customers meaningfully deferring Vault implementations, or is the slowdown concern concentrated in investor sentiment?
